svg.title: Two trivial steps, and one hidden assumption
svg.desc: Twelve points assigned to three cross-marked centres with dashed Voronoi boundaries, then the same points with the centres arrowed to their group means and ghosts left where they were, looped back by a curved repeat arrow annotated inertia 1200.2 to 566.9, beside three crossed-out failure panels for moon-shaped, anisotropic and unequal-variance data with adjusted Rand scores of 0.2549, 0.8995 and 0.8265 and their density- or mixture-model fixes, and a bottom pair showing the worse silhouette belongs to the better clustering.
svg.text: Two trivial steps, and one hidden assumption
(1) ASSIGN each point to the nearest centre
(2) UPDATE each centre to its group's mean
the big blob is cut in half
K-Means does not fail at random. It fails exactly
where that assumption is false - which you can see
the WORSE silhouette is the BETTER clustering. Internal metrics measure
geometry; only ARI knows the truth.
...and 10 million points? -> the answer surprises you
